payload.markdown: You have already encountered a situation in which the Mapper class displays a natural fault line. The createObject() method is used internally by Mapper, of course, but Collection objects also need it to create domain objects on demand. This requires us to pass along a Mapper reference when creating a Collection object. Although there’s nothing wrong with allowing callbacks (as you have seen in the Visitor and Observer patterns), it’s neater to move responsibility for domain object creation into its own type. This can then be shared by Mapper and Collection classes alike.

payload.markdown: Imagine a set of Mapper classes, broadly organized so that each faces its own domain object. The Domain Object Factory pattern simply requires that you extract the createObject() method from each Mapper and place it in its own class in a parallel hierarchy. Figure 13-6 shows these new classes.

items: Abstract Classes: A partial base class that forces subclasses to complete certain methods.
Callbacks: Functions handed to other functions, as in array_map and usort.
Classes & Objects: A class defines state and behaviour; objects are instances of that definition.
Factory Pattern: Creating objects through a dedicated creator instead of new at every call site.
Behavioral Patterns: Patterns that distribute responsibility and coordinate behaviour.

8579.title: Here’s a concrete implementation
8579.code:
<?php
class VenueObjectFactory extends DomainObjectFactory
{
    public function createObject(array $row): Venue
    {
        $obj = new Venue((int)$row['id'], $row['name']);

        return $obj;
    }
}
